marble.name: Counting objects to 20
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Count a set of objects to answer 'how many?' for sets up to 20 (arranged in lines, arrays, circles, or scattered)
marble.prompt: If you spread out 15 buttons on the table in a random arrangement and ask you how many there are, can they count them all carefully and give you the right answer?

cluster.summary: Your child is building essential counting skills — learning that numbers have meaning, that each number represents a specific quantity, and beginning to compare groups to see which has more or fewer objects.

misconceptions: Losing track on scattered sets → skips or double-counts (no tracking strategy).
Recounting when asked 'how many?' (cardinality not secure) or miscounting across the teens.
Treating teen numbers as unanalysable words rather than 'ten and some ones'.
Believing a rearranged set has a different total (conservation).
representations: Ten-frames (one full + a partial for teens).
Sets shown in line / array / circle / scattered (a deliberate arrangement ladder).
A numeral card matched to the counted set.
authoredAnswer: Tags each object once, keeps track of counted versus uncounted in the scattered set (moving or organising them), answers 'how many' with the last count word, and stops at exactly 13 when counting out.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: different totals on repeat counts of the scattered set; no strategy to keep place
wrongAnswers.fix: do NOT reteach counting as if the concept were missing — model a strategy: 'move each one over here as you count it', which is a tracking habit that develops with practice

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: fingers and words out of sync, giving an over- or under-count
wrongAnswers.fix: do NOT drill — slow to one touch per word, sliding each item aside; the coordination tightens with the move-it scaffold

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: keeps counting beyond 13 or gives all the counters
wrongAnswers.fix: state the target, count into a cupped hand, and stop-and-check — 'how many do we need? tell me when to stop'; this rebuilds the last-word-as-total link

before.name: How Many in Total?
before.reason: Answering 'how many?' requires the cardinality principle

before.name: One-to-one counting
